ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and point B is at the lower-right part of the circle. Through point B there is a tangent ray BC directed to the right, and point C is on this ray. There is also a segment/ray BA starting from B, passing through point A on the left side of the circle, and continuing to extend toward the upper left; BA is a ray on which a chord of the circle lies. The measure of minor arc AB is marked as 102° in the figure. The requested angle ABC is the obtuse angle formed at point B by BA and tangent BC. Reasoning: The measure of minor arc AB is known to be 102°. Angle ABC is the obtuse angle formed by tangent BC and chord BA, so it intercepts major arc AB. The measure of major arc AB is 360° - 102° = 258°. According to the tangent-chord theorem, the measure of the angle formed by a tangent and a chord is equal to half the measure of its intercepted arc, so m∠ABC = 258° / 2 = 129°.
